intended_object: The subgroup of GL_m(R) made of upper unitriangular matrices (upper triangular with all diagonal entries 1), i.e. the standard unipotent subgroup U of upper unitriangular matrices. The docstring and the name say this.
explanation:
The carrier is the set of invertible matrices g whose underlying matrix satisfies `IsUpperUnitriangular`. That predicate is defined in the library as Mathlib's `IsUpperTriangular` (M i j = 0 whenever j < i) together with M i i = 1 for every i. This is exactly the textbook set of upper unitriangular matrices.

The setting is general enough:
- R can be any ring, not necessarily commutative.
- m can be any finite, linearly ordered index type. Finiteness is needed for GL, and a linear order is the standard setting for triangularity.

The subgroup axioms are proved, so the definition yields the intended subgroup. A degenerate case also comes out right: for empty m the subgroup is the trivial group.

I searched Mathlib for a ready-made unitriangular, unipotent or Borel subgroup of GL. It has none; the only near match is the line-stabilizer "unipotent radical" in the PSL file, which is a different object. So the definition is faithful.
